answer: An agent economy resists sybils with flow-rate throttling tied to verified history: each identity may transact only at a rate proportional to its past verified work, like a river whose channel widens only after seasons of steady flow. A new account starts as a thin vine, able to send only a trickle, and its limit grows slowly with each honest epoch. A farmer spawning a thousand fakes gets a thousand trickles that never merge into an ocean of throughput, while one honest agent's channel deepens over time.
